title: MiniMax H3 short-drama episode storyboard
description: Input for scripts/validate_episode.py and scripts/build_prompts.py. Asset references in text use {asset_id} placeholders; <Subject N>/<Picture N> labels are assigned at build time in wiring order (characters, scene, props, then audio).

style.description: Opening style sentence reused by every segment unless overridden

identity_phrase.description: English noun phrase "a <who> with <features>": what tells this person apart at a glance - hair, main garment and colour, one marker (about 12-25 words). Written into every prompt; repeated where the person first appears.

short_phrase.description: How prompts call this person: "the grey-haired doctor in the white coat". Default: "the" + the head of identity_phrase ("the man in his fifties"). People are never called by name in a prompt.

pronoun.description: For sentences the builder writes itself ("closes his lips"). Default: read from the head of identity_phrase (man / woman ...), else "they".

sheet_phrase.description: The full look used only to GENERATE the reference pictures (face structure, build, height ...). Never written into a video prompt.

reference_images.description: face, outfit/full body, optional detail; paths relative to this JSON

voice_reference.description: 2–15 s clean speech; attached only in segments where the character speaks

name_en.description: English name for people reading the files. Prompts never use a person's name (see short_phrase).

description.description: Written once, pasted unchanged; no people

reference_images.description: Paths are relative to the folder of this JSON; paths relative to the project root (where the scripts are run) are accepted too.

name_en.description: English label used inside prompts (the display `name` may be Chinese). Default: `name` when it is ASCII, otherwise derived from the id (xu_qing -> Xu Qing, prop_old_key -> the old key)

reference_images.description: A prop without an image WILL be invented by the model Paths are relative to the folder of this JSON; paths relative to the project root (where the scripts are run) are accepted too.

rarity.description: UI tier overlaid in post, never rendered

name_en.description: English label used inside prompts (the display `name` may be Chinese). Default: `name` when it is ASCII, otherwise derived from the id (xu_qing -> Xu Qing, prop_old_key -> the old key)

duration.description: Seconds; snapped to the 17k+5 frame grid at build time

hook_type.description: Planning label only (hook / setup / turn / cliffhanger); never written into the prompt

continuity.description: The state the segment opens from, written as a state (who is where, facing what, holding what, light) with {asset_id} placeholders; leave empty for the first segment. "@observed" (optionally followed by wardrobe / light notes) opens from where the previous segment's ACCEPTED take really ended: build_prompts.py inserts that segment's observed_end_state and refuses to build until it exists (--allow-planned for drafts)

end_state.description: The room-wide state at the end of the segment (positions, facing, props held, light), written as a state with {asset_id} placeholders, no trailing period. Always describe everyone present, even when the last shot is an insert - it is the hand-off for the next segment (the builder leaves it out of the prompt when the segment closes on an insert)

accepted_take.description: The take that was accepted for this segment; written by observe_take.py

observed_end_state.description: Where the accepted take really ends, read from its last frames (never copied from end_state). Same style as end_state, {asset_id} placeholders

observation_confidence.description: How sure the frames make the observer; low triggers a validator warning

accepted_deviations.description: What differs from the planned end_state and was accepted anyway

negatives.description: Appended verbatim to the description. Write it as a positive lock sentence (e.g. the corridor stays empty), never as a bare 'no X'

start.description: Seconds within the segment; shot 1 must be 0; each shot ≥ 1.2 s

camera.description: One dominant move in official vocabulary, as a sentence

action.description: ≥ 8 words, starting state → movement → ending state (a closing period is optional; no looks, no speech verbs)

offscreen.description: Voice-over or a voice from someone who is not seen: written as an off-screen voiceover with every mouth on screen closed. The speaker then need not be in the segment's character_ids.

after_line.description: Optional full sentence: what the speaker does right after the words end ("He closes his lips and lowers his eyes to {prop_folder}."). Default: the speaker closes the lips.

en.description: Optional English subtitle for this line (used by retime_subtitles.py / export_capcut_draft.py --bilingual). Never spoken, never written into the prompt.

lens.description: Optional focal length / depth of field, e.g. '35mm, shallow depth of field'

lighting.description: Optional per-shot key light direction, colour temperature, practicals; inherits the scene when empty

performance.description: Optional trigger -> reception -> one primary response -> settled; ≤3 observable cues per beat

sound_cue.description: Optional single diegetic sound tied to an action in this shot

end_hold.description: Last shot of the segment: settle 0.5 s then hold 1 s (trimmed at assembly)

first_frame_prompt.description: For a segment that gets a generated first frame (any mode, including ref2va + first_frame): English still-image prompt for the literal first frame (see assets/image-prompts.md)

summary.description: Optional: one English sentence saying what happens in the segment ({asset_id} placeholders allowed); goes into the prompt's summary section

use_scene_reference.description: False: do not attach the scene picture for this segment (a scene reference roughly halves camera movement); the scene description text carries the place

stagings.description: Optional. Opening positions for a scene: one entry per scene visit, bound to the first segment of that visit. build_prompts.py turns it into one fixed blocking sentence at the start of that segment, so positions are stated the same way every time. Later segments in the scene inherit through continuity / "@observed".

segment.description: id of the first segment of this scene visit

character.description: character id; only people present when the scene opens (who enters later is not listed)

at.description: What they are next to, as a phrase that follows the verb: "at the left end of the grey sofa", "by the door"; use things the scene master actually shows, or a position relative to another placed person ("two steps behind {lao_chen}")

side.description: side of the frame in the scene's main camera axis

posture.description: a verb in the third person: stands / sits / kneels / leans / crouches / lies

places.description: Who is already there when the scene opens (may be empty when everybody walks in)

others.description: a positive statement about the rest of the space: "the other seats stay empty"

enters_later.description: Characters of this segment who are not there at the start and walk in during it
